title: Blockchain Developer Roadmap
summary: Build from programming and databases into cryptography, distributed systems, smart contracts, blockchain protocols, decentralized applications and secure production deployment.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and completing around 2030. Use each semester as a separate learning and portfolio milestone.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: develop strong programming, blockchain fundamentals, smart-contract and dApp skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: specialise in smart contracts, protocol engineering, blockchain infrastructure, security or Web3 applications.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: move toward protocol architecture, blockchain security, distributed systems or technical leadership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: maintain expertise in distributed systems, cryptography, security, scalability and emerging decentralised infrastructure.

rows.text: C/C++ or Java/Python fundamentals, Git, data structures and algorithms
30+ programming exercises and a documented Git repository
Networking, databases, operating systems and basic cryptography
MDN Web Docs · NIST Cryptographic Standards
Build a small client/server application and document authentication/encryption concepts
Blockchain architecture, hashing, digital signatures, wallets, transactions and consensus
Implement a simplified blockchain locally with blocks, hashes and validation
Deploy a simple token or escrow contract on a test network
dApps, JavaScript/TypeScript, wallets, RPC and frontend integration
Full-stack dApp connecting a frontend, wallet and smart contract
Smart-contract testing, security, gas optimisation and common vulnerabilities
Audit your own contract and publish a vulnerability report
Advanced distributed systems, L2/scaling concepts, indexing and blockchain infrastructure
Production-style project with indexing, monitoring and automated tests
2 polished projects, security report, GitHub portfolio and internship applications

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If your university offers a four-year honours route, use the additional depth for protocol research, distributed-systems work, blockchain security research, open-source contributions or an extended industry project.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Keep the technical foundation broader than a single blockchain framework. Distributed systems, cryptography, networking, databases, security and systems programming remain transferable even if particular chains, protocols or development frameworks change.

blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: PhD routes

Maintain a systems-level foundation rather than tying your career to one blockchain ecosystem. Distributed systems, cryptography, security, networking, databases and formal methods provide longer-term technical foundations for protocol engineering and security work.
